2609.01386.title: When Tokenization is Secretly Output Supervision
2609.01386.paper_summary: Tokenization in language models is treated by default as an input preprocessing decision. We argue that this framing is incomplete: in autoregressive models, tokenizer granularity determines what the model must resolve in a single forward pass, and therefore the supervision signal it receives. This affects both the difficulty of the learning problem and the representations that emerge inside the model. We test this in a controlled experiment on numeric reasoning with a novel decoupling of input and output tokenization. As the output supervision view predicts, differences in task performance, training dynamics, and model internals are induced by output tokenization and largely invariant to input tokenization. This may matter in practice, because models with different tokenization strategies differ not only in input representation but in the task they were trained on. Comparisons between models may thus partly reflect task definition rather than ability. A survey of 120 recent *CL papers on numeric reasoning confirms that this is rarely acknowledged: only about 10% report the numeric tokenization of the models they evaluate, while 69% compare across tokenization, and thus supervision, regimes without reporting it. While prior work documents that tokenization consistently affects model performance, there is no principled account of why. We argue that framing tokenization as output supervision provides that account.
2609.01386.paper_summary_zh: 語言模型中的標記化預設被視為一種輸入預處理決策。<lb/>我們認為這種框架是不完整的：在自回歸模型中，標記器的粒度決定了模型在單次前向傳播中必須解決的問題，因此也決定了它所接收的監督信號。<lb/>這影響了學習問題的難度以及模型內部出現的表徵。<lb/>我們在一個受控實驗中測試這一點，該實驗涉及數字推理，並對輸入和輸出標記化進行了新穎的解耦。<lb/>正如輸出監督視角所預測的，任務表現、訓練動態和模型內部的差異是由輸出標記化引起的，並且在很大程度上與輸入標記化無關。<lb/>這在實踐中可能很重要，因為具有不同標記化策略的模型不僅在輸入表徵上有所不同，還在它們所訓練的任務上有所不同。<lb/>因此，模型之間的比較可能部分反映了任務定義而非能力。<lb/>對120篇近期*CL數字推理論文的調查確認，這一點很少被承認：只有約10%報告了他們評估的模型的數字標記化，而69%在未報告的情況下比較了標記化，因此監督，的範疇。<lb/>雖然先前的研究記錄了標記化始終影響模型性能，但並沒有原則性的解釋為什麼。<lb/>我們認為將標記化框架作為輸出監督提供了這一解釋。
